A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Stay-Positive research, with matching authors, method, and core experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original detector-training experiments, compression and resizing tests, inpainting detection, and appendix evaluations on GenImage, GAN-generated images, and real-image domains.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds quantitative training ablations, corruption tests, SynthBuster resizing evaluations, and UFD benchmark results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the frozen backbone, ReLU features, binary cross-entropy objective, and final-layer retraining with weights clamped to nonnegative values. The newly evaluated clamp-only and whole-network variants are ablation controls; the proposed procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation coverage through the UFD benchmark, including pixel-space diffusion generators GLIDE and ADM and autoregressive DALL-E. It also adds SynthBuster resizing tests across several generators, including SDXL. The earlier latent-generator, inpainting, GenImage, GAN, and real-domain coverage is retained.

E2.justification: AEROBLADE becomes an evaluated zero-shot comparator in Table 2; v1 discussed it only in related work. The other comparator rows in that experiment and the existing GenImage and GAN comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce controlled comparisons of retraining scope and corruption-strength sweeps with separate real/fake score reporting. v2 also adds equally weighted averages across generators. For retained experiments, Appendix A.1 changes the reported retraining batch size from 2048 to 1024, Figure 4 revises the WEBP quality scale, and several diagnostic plots are described as logits instead of probabilities. These reported revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 and Table 4 newly quantify whether clamping alone or whole-network retraining can replace frozen-backbone last-layer retraining; v1 only discussed the whole-network alternative qualitatively. Appendix A.3 adds JPEG, Gaussian-noise, and low-pass-filtering analyses, plus resizing robustness on SynthBuster. These substantially expand the evidence testing design choices and robustness.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1 in both versions reports averages across two trained networks. No additional runs, seed identifiers, confidence intervals, significance tests, or newly specified uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported. Shaded plots and distribution visualizations occur in both versions.

E6.justification: v2 adds AEROBLADE scores, ablation results, UFD benchmark results, corruption and SynthBuster curves, and aggregate averages. For example, new Table 6 reports ADM AP of 44.51 for Corvi and 74.52 for Corvi⊕. The earlier per-generator entries in Tables 1–3 and the matched GenImage/GAN tables remain unchanged. Some added averages are inconsistent: Table 2 swaps the UFD-ProGAN and UFD-LDM row averages.

T1.justification: The ReLU/sigmoid assumptions, score decomposition, and sign-based definitions of real and fake features are unchanged. The toy argument about detecting the absence of WEBP artifacts is retained from v1 Appendix A.4 as v2 Appendix A.6, without new mathematical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that ignoring real-associated features through nonnegative last-layer retraining improves generalization, post-processing robustness, and inpainting detection. The added experiments support these retained claims. The new audio/video remark is explicitly a future research possibility, not a demonstrated contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations attributing clamp-only failures to inadequate feature reweighting and whole-network failures to newly learned spurious fake features. It interprets similar corruption robustness in light of training augmentations and explicitly recommends more careful dataset curation. The conclusion adds tentative applicability to audio/video; the existing limitations concerning spurious fake features remain.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a project-page link for implementation details. Appendix A.1 newly reports approximately 15 epochs and four additional hours for second-stage training, and revises its batch size from 2048 to 1024. Most augmentation, validation, stopping, and inference details are retained. The PDFs alone do not verify the linked resources' availability.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds focused positioning against Liu et al. (2021) and Kirichenko et al. (2023), distinguishing their second-stage data curation from Stay-Positive's weight constraints. ZeroFake and references for newly evaluated generators are also added. Most remaining citation changes, including Rajan's title/year update, concern the same previously cited works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized revisions to the introduction, limitations, related work, and conclusion, adds experimental subsections, and renumbers the appendix around new material. It also updates the conference header and bibliography formatting. The overall narrative order and most methodological exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds ablation and UFD tables, multi-panel corruption and SynthBuster figures, and average columns in existing tables. Figure 4's WEBP axis changes, while Figures 7, 9, and the GAN real-distribution plot are relabeled with logit scores. Several retained appendix figures move into a concluding figure block, producing substantial display and layout changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The quantitative ablations, broader generator tests, and corruption analyses strengthen support for the training design and its applicability; implementation-cost disclosure and closer prior-work positioning also help. These gains are limited by new reporting problems: Table 2 swaps the UFD averages and reports Rajan⊕ as 96.96 versus 97.28 in Table 4 despite identical component scores. Unexplained probability-to-logit relabeling also leaves diagnostic score interpretation unclear. Overall, the added evidence provides a modest net improvement.
